Relative transfer update: default/length GetBytes append to destination WriterIndex without growing; default/length SetBytes consume source ReaderIndex without changing destination indices; default ReadBytes fills destination WritableBytes and moves both cursors; explicit-destination ReadBytes moves only source ReaderIndex; default WriteBytes consumes all readable source bytes; explicit-source WriteBytes grows destination and moves only its WriterIndex. All return the receiver, keep marks/reference counts, and delegate to the existing bounded bulk kernel. Explicit source write grows before source-range validation, as in Java. Failed copies publish no cursor changes but may leave increased capacity or partially changed composite bytes. Existing CLR snapshot/memmove overlap policy applies; Java can repeat overwritten bytes across composite self-copy boundaries. Default reads check destination lifetime before computing WritableBytes to retain IllegalReferenceCountException after native/heap storage is cleared on final release; Java reports bounds/argument errors in two such probes. Null arguments use early ArgumentNullException. Byte[] ranges remain native Span slices rather than duplicated Java array overloads. Policy: docs/buffer-porting.md#relative-buffer-transfers. Decoder storage/read update: ReadBytes(length) now uses the creator allocator Buffer factory instead of forcing a raw heap owner. It advances source ReaderIndex only after successful copy and initializes only the result readable range even if the allocator reserves extra capacity. Failed copies retain CLR result cleanup; pinned Java readBytes lacks that cleanup. Zero/invalid reads do not allocate. Policy: docs/buffer-porting.md#decoder-storage-hints-and-allocated-reads. Pooled heap consumer: both EnsureWritable overloads now use MaxFastWritableBytes before the creator allocator growth hook, preserving existing normalized reservations as pinned Java requires. Unpooled defaults remain WritableBytes. Automatic leak integration: the combined ByteBuf type captures one factory-created ResourceLeakDetector<ByteBuf> at explicit CLR type initialization (including an empty sentinel), as the shared skeletal detector. Configure the factory before buffers/allocators; later replacement does not change it. All wrappers and supported allocator factories share this detector. Remaining source surfaces stay partial. Diagnostic update: The combined CLR kernel implements the original metadata/freed/unwrapped diagnostic without content reads or freed capacity/unwrap access. Whole source/fixture remains partial. Size-query update: CanRead(int) preserves original readable-index comparison, including nonpositive counts without validation; shared EmptyByteBuf always returns false. Transparent ordinary/composite/unreleasable facades forward virtual queries without leak recording. CanWrite(int) no longer rejects negative counts before its original comparison; read-only and empty-sentinel results remain false. Current CLR fixed-derived read-only policy is retained. Whole source remains partial. Socket channel update: connected Socket overloads preserve absolute cursors and publish relative cursors only by successful actual counts. Send/Receive execute once; synchronous WouldBlock becomes zero, EOF becomes zero, other socket errors propagate. Empty ranges validate buffer/null/permissions but skip socket I/O, including disposed sockets. Composite input uses one staged receive instead of Java repeated component reads. Snapshots/staging use O(length) pooled managed storage, not zero-copy gather/scatter; caller excludes concurrent mutation/release/external cursor changes. Failed input I/O publishes no staging; later composite commit may change a prefix. Async directly awaits Socket Memory-based operations; pre-cancellation follows validation and precedes growth, successful results commit despite late cancellation, growth survives failure/EOF, and async readiness waits rather than returning sync WouldBlock. Socket ownership/reference counts are borrowed. New unrelated-reference overloads require typed nulls to disambiguate from Stream; five existing stream null tests now specify Stream. Four original public Java comments and licenses are retained. This covers connected network channel I/O, not arbitrary custom Java channels or provider-specific native I/O. Scalar-dispatch update: public absolute parent delegates are distinct from bounded relative/slice kernels. Owned pooled duplicates preserve the pinned LongLE relative public-setter path; floating/boolean/char/signed-medium relative APIs preserve their integer composition and upstream receiver-return rules. CLR byte values are unsigned wire octets; existing Span/memory hooks replace JVM per-primitive protected kernel topology, including safe-direct medium byte callbacks. docs/buffer-porting.md#derived-scalar-dispatch.

GetString/ReadString/SetString/WriteString use Encoding/ReadOnlySpan<char>, exact reservation, no implicit preamble and caller fallback policy; Java malformed/single-byte/BOM behavior is explicitly adapted (docs/buffer-porting.md). ReadString enforces the original documented readable bound; zero-length indexed access and BytesBefore are consistently checked. Func<byte,bool> replaces ByteProcessor; callbacks reacquire storage after mutation. Remaining I/O, utility and broader APIs are pending. Read-only views add IsReadOnly/AsReadOnly and native CanWrite. Getters, source transfers, decoding, searches and copies use bounded ReadOnlyMemory/Span; mutable borrows/writes use permission guards. Read-only DiscardSomeReadBytes retains the original index-only consumed-buffer reset. I/O and remaining utilities still pending. Composite consumer adds bounded segment hooks, stack crossing-word access, borrowed ReadOnlySequence, and cross-component bulk/overlap/text/search/view behavior. Contiguous memory borrowing never silently copies; unsupported multi-segment Memory ranges are actual CLR representation limits. Standalone ReadBytes now follows creator allocator Buffer policy; see decoder storage/read update below. Unreleasable consumer requires transparent shared indices and marks: private ref-return access routes to the captured index owner without an extra state allocation. Ordinary owners/slices/duplicates still own independent state. Slice/retained/read-slice/duplicate conveniences and AsReadOnly are virtual so lifetime-suppressing wrappers can preserve the original derived-view contract. Full existing Buffer suite is rerun for this base change. Synchronous stream transfer update: inherited GetBytes/SetBytes/ReadBytes/WriteBytes overloads accept a borrowed System.IO.Stream. Absolute operations preserve indices, relative output advances reader only after complete success, and relative input pre-reserves the requested length then advances writer by the actual returned count. All storage kinds perform one bounded Stream.Read, returning short reads immediately and EOF as 0; this deliberately replaces the Java CompositeByteBuf fill-until-EOF loop and prevents retrying CLR EOF forever. Zero lengths validate buffer/range/permission/null without calling the stream. Pooled staging avoids native-span lifetime across callbacks, snapshots all output before a single Stream.Write, and prevents a throwing input from publishing its temporary bytes; unlike Java heap reads, input I/O failure leaves target contents unchanged. A later composite storage-commit failure can still modify earlier writable components, leaving writer unchanged, and source input can already be consumed. Streams and buffer references remain borrowed. Input staging rechecks destination permission/range after callbacks. Temporary memory is proportional to requested length plus pool bucket rounding, and copying is deliberate; no zero-copy/performance claim. Concurrent changes, release, and external mutation of the active cursor during I/O remain caller exclusions; same-buffer append with the supplied stream adapters is tested. Channel/positioned-file and async ByteBuf transfer APIs remain pending. Async stream transfer update: GetBytesAsync/SetBytesAsync/ReadBytesAsync/WriteBytesAsync are CLR counterparts of the four synchronous stream contracts, using ValueTask, CancellationToken and the stream Memory-based asynchronous operations directly. Managed pooled staging survives suspension; no native memory is borrowed across await. One bounded input read, EOF=0, borrowed lifetime and success-only index publication follow the synchronous CLR policy. Pre-cancellation follows argument/permission validation and prevents growth/I/O; started growth is not rolled back. A valid stream result commits despite late token cancellation; a thrown cancellation or failure leaves active indices unchanged and does not publish staged input. Callers must keep streams/buffers alive and exclude concurrent mutation and external active-cursor changes through completion. Full cancellation, failure, alias and partial composite-commit limits: docs/buffer-porting.md#asynchronous-stream-transfers. Channel/positioned-file APIs and broader original source remain pending. Positioned file update: SafeFileHandle plus System.IO.RandomAccess map all four FileChannel absolute/relative overloads without changing file position; four ValueTask/CancellationToken forms are CLR async extensions. Successful CLR writes complete the requested range and return length (Java permits partial write counts); one bounded read returns actual bytes with EOF=0 across all backing kinds. Closed handles throw rather than Java input -1; invalid/closed/null handles, negative ranges and signed file-end overflow are validated even for zero requests, before growth/I/O. Absolute operations preserve indices; relative indices publish only after success. Output uses a pooled snapshot; input commits managed staging after reading, with async destination revalidation and no native borrow across await. Read failures do not publish staging, but later composite commit failures can change earlier components; failed output may partially change the file while leaving reader unchanged. Input reserves requested capacity before actual I/O, preserving growth on EOF/error; pre-cancellation follows validation and prevents growth/I/O. Buffer/handle ownership is borrowed through completion, without implicit Retain/disposal; exclude concurrent buffer mutation/release and external active-cursor changes. Full semantics, limitations and evidence: docs/buffer-porting.md#positioned-file-transfers. Gathering/scattering channel consumer mapping and broader APIs remain pending. Content comparison/hash update: original equality/hash/comparison API comments are retained in ByteBuf.Comparison.cs. Native IEquatable<ByteBuf>/IComparable<ByteBuf>, Equals/GetHashCode and default sorting replace Java Object/Comparable contracts; == stays reference identity. CompareTo(null)=1 follows CLR sorting. Readable content determines values; hash keys require stable bytes/indices/lifetime. Full policy: docs/buffer-porting.md#content-comparison-and-hashing. Allocator policy update: creator IByteBufAllocator is retained through owners, derived/read-only/unreleasable views and allocator-specific empty buffers. Both writable-growth paths consult its capacity hook; heap/native copies and composite padding/consolidation/copies use its factories. Legacy explicit native reservation domains remain in effect for subsequent copies and composite allocations. Existing Unpooled heap/native defaults are preserved. Policy and limits: docs/buffer-porting.md#allocator-policy-foundation. ByteBufConvertible integration: all buffer kinds implement IByteBufConvertible through inherited AsByteBuf, which returns this without changing references or requiring accessible storage. Original conversion operation comment retained. Buffer-holder consumers inherit existing buffer content/hash/copy/lifetime policies; whole source stays partial. Policy: docs/buffer-porting.md#buffer-holders-and-conversion. Relative transfer update: default/length GetBytes append to destination WriterIndex without growing; default/length SetBytes consume source ReaderIndex without changing destination indices; default ReadBytes fills destination WritableBytes and moves both cursors; explicit-destination ReadBytes moves only source ReaderIndex; default WriteBytes consumes all readable source bytes; explicit-source WriteBytes grows destination and moves only its WriterIndex. All return the receiver, keep marks/reference counts, and delegate to the existing bounded bulk kernel. Explicit source write grows before source-range validation, as in Java. Failed copies publish no cursor changes but may leave increased capacity or partially changed composite bytes. Existing CLR snapshot/memmove overlap policy applies; Java can repeat overwritten bytes across composite self-copy boundaries. Default reads check destination lifetime before computing WritableBytes to retain IllegalReferenceCountException after native/heap storage is cleared on final release; Java reports bounds/argument errors in two such probes. Null arguments use early ArgumentNullException. Byte[] ranges remain native Span slices rather than duplicated Java array overloads. Policy: docs/buffer-porting.md#relative-buffer-transfers. Both original API comments are preserved. ReadBytes(length) now allocates through Allocator.Buffer(length, MaxCapacity), preserving creator policy, metrics and independent ownership; zero reads keep the shared empty sentinel. Failed copies release the new result before rethrowing, retaining the existing CLR cleanup beyond the pinned Java implementation. Policy: docs/buffer-porting.md#decoder-storage-hints-and-allocated-reads. Async signatures remain native virtual ValueTask operations. Policy: docs/buffer-porting.md#advanced-leak-aware-buffer-access-records. Transparent ordinary/composite/unreleasable facades forward virtual queries without leak recording. CanWrite(int) no longer rejects negative counts before its original comparison; read-only and empty-sentinel results remain false. Current CLR fixed-derived read-only policy is retained. Whole source remains partial. Socket channel update: connected Socket overloads preserve absolute cursors and publish relative cursors only by successful actual counts. Send/Receive execute once; synchronous WouldBlock becomes zero, EOF becomes zero, other socket errors propagate. This intentionally removes Java order metadata, wrapper/cache identity, order(null) validation and wrapper diagnostic names. Cursor/mark/capacity/reference operations act on the same selected buffer; a second index owner is not created. Explicit LE methods always remain LE, even when Java unsuffixed access was selected BE/LE. UInt16/UInt32 model unsigned results; char uses a UTF-16 UInt16 unit, and Single/Double use raw Int32/Int64 bit conversions. Existing Memory/Span/ReadOnlySequence plus scoped pins replace ordered NIO views and exposed address/array metadata. Comparisons/hash use canonical content through ByteBufUtil. Other methods are order-neutral forwarding: call the underlying CLR ByteBuf operation; its remaining APIs are tracked on their own entries. Future codec/transport order consumers must choose accessors explicitly; no automatic Java source compatibility is claimed.

Leading unreadable ByteBuf references are released, while the subsequent array suffix owns even empty buffers and safely releases entries after null. Byte arrays skip empties and stop at null. Limits trigger one final heap consolidation, including the original readonly-to-writable copied result; native source flags/permissions survive until copying. On factory failure, already acquired prefix ownership is released because no composite can be returned; untransferred preflight suffix ownership remains with callers. Copying update: byte[]/ReadOnlySpan copies, array subregions, single ByteBuf and params byte[][]/ByteBuf[] copies produce independent writable heap storage without moving source indices/marks or consuming/retaining input references. Array/Span and multiple-input results have a fixed maximum equal to copied length; a single ByteBuf (including an array of one ByteBuf) uses the original growable heap result. This corrects the earlier Span factory maximum of int.MaxValue. Null entries throw instead of terminating copying. Total-length preflight uses subtraction before addition and rejects repeated shared-backing overflow before allocation. Empty-only input returns the shared sentinel without ownership changes; a mixed readable/empty input still performs original zero-length source-access checks. Byte order is explicit BE/LE operations, so the JVM mutable-order reconciliation is omitted while raw bytes are preserved and its original documentation retained with CLR remarks. Single-source failure releases the new output; merged ownership is published only after every read succeeds. Empty region bounds/null checks follow the existing CLR wrapping adaptation. Text-copying update: string and char[] whole/range overloads plus ReadOnlySpan<char> replace CharSequence/CharBuffer and encode into independent writable growable heap ownership. Whole empty strings retain independent growable ownership; empty ranges/arrays/spans return the shared sentinel. Nonempty text encoded to zero bytes by empty fallback still owns a growable buffer. Null encoding and empty region bounds are validated, unlike original early-empty shortcuts. Sizing failure allocates nothing; write failure releases the new owner before rethrowing. Primitive-copying update: all 15 original scalar/array CopyInt/CopyShort/CopyMedium/CopyLong/CopyBoolean/CopyFloat/CopyDouble operations are implemented, including both short[] and int[] CopyShort forms. Nonempty copies own writable heap storage, use exact initial capacity, and can grow to int.MaxValue. Output is big-endian regardless of host order; Short/Medium discard upper bits, bool emits 0/1, and float/double preserve raw IEEE bits rather than canonicalizing NaNs. External-memory copying update: single ReadOnlyMemory and params ReadOnlyMemory[] overloads copy selected ranges into independent writable heap roots at reader 0/writer copied length, with maximum equal to that length. Multiple-memory wrapping update: writable and read-only Memory-array overloads, with optional explicit maximum components, now port the NIO wrapping factories. A single supplied range uses its single wrapper and ignores an unused component limit. Default Memory is empty and skipped, so Java nullable-element termination has no Memory-value equivalent; null arrays are rejected. Static delegates replace Java ByteWrapper without an intermediate ByteBuf array. Complete the batch before consolidation. External owners are neither retained nor disposed; failure releases only temporary wrappers and owned consolidation results. Read-only components reject writes until owned writable heap consolidation; composite IsReadOnly follows ordinary Java composite policy. Mixing mutability remains available through existing ByteBuf[] wrapping. This supersedes the earlier multi-memory wrapping pending note; provider-specific/raw-address and other remaining factories remain pending. Policy: docs/buffer-porting.md#multiple-external-memory-wrapping. Decoder storage/read update: The private unknown-MemoryManager wrapper reports contiguous storage because one Memory range represents one region, without inferring native storage or taking ownership of its manager. Native-address update: original raw-address factory is now WrappedBuffer(nint,int,bool), with original operation comment. MemoryManager/SafeHandle replace JVM direct buffers/Unsafe. Optional NativeMemory.Free ownership is transferred only after successful construction; borrowed pointers require external lifetime throughout access/pins. Capacity changes detach to existing owned-native allocation with rollback on failure. External address ranges do not charge reservations/factory metrics, and pins defer owned free after logical final release/detachment. Common source is unchanged. Whole source remains partial.
